The linear models of Study 2 (`3_linearmodels.qmd`) give every participant
their own effects of task difficulty and of illusion strength, and of the two
together, on each parameter of the DDM. This script asks how reliable these
participant-level effects are: how well they tell the participants apart,
given how uncertain each participant's estimate is. Those that do are the
candidates for measuring individual differences in sensitivity to illusions.

Like the other scripts, it never loads a fit. The participants' effects are
summarised on the cluster, from the draws of the best linear model of each
illusion (`compute_grouplevel()` in `server/predictions.R`, run by
`./hpc predict`), and stored in the model's prediction file, which is pulled
with `./hpc pull predictions`. The full fits hold some 70,000 participant-level
parameters each, and were made with brms 2.21.0 (`server/AGENT.md` §3.9).

::: {.callout-warning}
**For now this runs on the 50-participant test of the Müller-Lyer model**
(untransformed, `server/AGENT.md` §6.15): the pipeline, not the results. Fifty
participants estimate neither the variability between participants nor the
reliability well, and the Vertical-Horizontal and Ebbinghaus models are not
fitted yet.
:::

## Loading

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| error: false

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

# igc_grouplevel_effects: the definitions of the participants' effects
source(if (dir.exists("server")) "server/predictions.R" else "analysis/server/predictions.R")
# igc_linear_ranges: the linear subrange, which the empirical indices are
# computed over, as the models are fitted over it
source(if (dir.exists("server")) "server/models.R" else "analysis/server/models.R")

path <- if (dir.exists("models")) "models/" else "analysis/models/"
data_path <- if (dir.exists("../data")) "../data/" else "data/"

# The prediction file of the best linear model of each illusion: the variant
# (untransformed or transformed, 3_linearmodels.qmd) that the comparison of
# the fits retains. Until the full fits exist, the Müller-Lyer one is the
# 50-participant test of 2026-11-25 (job 11841190, server/AGENT.md 6.15), in a
# directory of its own (pulled with IGC_LOCAL_MODELS, server/hpc), untransformed
# (the user's choice over the √|strength| test, 2026-11-25), and the
# Vertical-Horizontal one the same test of that illusion. An illusion with no
# file yet is left out.
best_files <- c(
  MullerLyer = paste0(path, "test_lin_ddm5_20261125_nutpie/predictions/lin_ddm5_mullerlyer_MullerLyer.rds"),
  VerticalHorizontal = paste0(path, "test_lin_ddm5_20261125_nutpie/predictions/",
                              "lin_ddm5_verticalhorizontal_VerticalHorizontal.rds")
)

illusions <- c(MullerLyer = "Müller-Lyer", VerticalHorizontal = "Vertical-Horizontal",
               Ebbinghaus = "Ebbinghaus")
# The model's parameters, as estimate_grouplevel() names them ("conditional"
# is the drift)
parameter_labels <- c(conditional = "Drift", sigmadrift = "Drift Variability", boundary = "Boundary",
                      bias = "Starting Point", ndt = "Non-Decision Time", poutlier = "Outlier Proportion")

best_files <- best_files[file.exists(best_files)]
if (length(best_files) < length(illusions)) {
  message("No linear model yet for: ", paste(setdiff(names(illusions), names(best_files)), collapse = ", "))
}
grouplevel <- imap(best_files, \(file, ill) {
  p <- readRDS(file)
  if (is.null(p$grouplevel)) {
    message(file, " has no participants' effects: re-run `./hpc predict` (predictions.R since 2026-11-25).")
  }
  p$grouplevel
})
grouplevel <- grouplevel[!vapply(grouplevel, is.null, logical(1))]

# The tables, in one style, with the numbers centred in their cells
gt_style <- function(tab) {
  tab |>
    cols_align("center", columns = where(is.numeric)) |>
    tab_options(table.font.size = px(13), heading.title.font.size = px(16),
                heading.subtitle.font.size = px(13), data_row.padding = px(3),
                row_group.font.weight = "bold", row_group.background.color = "#F5F5F5")
}
```

## The Participants' Effects

Each parameter of the linear models has, per participant, a deviation from the
population for each of its terms (the random effects): an intercept, the
difference, the absolute strength, the absolute strength by its direction
(Effect, +0.5 when the illusion is incongruent, −0.5 when it is congruent),
and the interactions of the difference with the last two. The raw terms are
not the most interpretable, since the effect of the strength is split between
`Strength` and `Strength:Effect`. The effects studied here are the baseline of
each parameter (its intercept) and combinations of the other terms, made draw
by draw on the cluster:

```{r}
effect_meanings <- c(
  "Baseline" = "The parameter with no illusion, at the middle difficulty and the centre of the ISI window",
  "Difficulty" = "The effect of the difference between the targets, with no illusion",
  "Strength (incongruent)" = "The slope of the illusion's strength when it is incongruent",
  "Strength (congruent)" = "The slope of the illusion's strength when it is congruent",
  "Difficulty x Strength (incongruent)" = "How the difference changes the slope of an incongruent illusion",
  "Difficulty x Strength (congruent)" = "How the difference changes the slope of a congruent illusion",
  "PSE" = paste0("The difference between the targets at which the drift is zero under an incongruent illusion ",
                 "of medium strength: the difference the illusion cancels (drift only, raw units)")
)
tibble(Effect = names(igc_grouplevel_effects),
       Terms = map_chr(igc_grouplevel_effects, \(w) {
         paste(sprintf("%s%s%s", ifelse(seq_along(w) == 1, "", ifelse(w < 0, " − ", " + ")),
                       ifelse(abs(w) == 1, "", paste0(abs(w), " × ")), names(w)), collapse = "")
       })) |>
  add_row(Effect = "PSE",
          Terms = "−a / g in raw units: a, g the total drift at D = 0 and its slope of D, at half the strongest strength") |>
  mutate(Meaning = effect_meanings[Effect]) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "The participants' effects", subtitle = "Per parameter of the model") |>
  gt_style() |>
  cols_align("left")
```

The predictors are coded as in the fits: the difference from −1 to 1 and the
absolute strength from 0 to 1 over the range fitted, so the slope of the
strength is the change from no illusion to the strongest illusion of the range.
Each effect is a deviation of the participant from the population, on the
link scale of its parameter, and the baseline a deviation from the
participant's study, which has an intercept of its own. The outlier proportion
has a baseline only. Baselines can be expected to be the most reliable: every
trial informs them, where a slope rests on the contrast between trials.

The model-based PSE is the one effect that is not a deviation. It is computed
draw by draw from the participant's total coefficients on the drift
(population + study + participant), in the raw units of the difference, at
the same strength as the empirical PSE below (`igc_pse_strength`, half the
strongest of the range). It is the illusion's strength expressed as the
physical difference it cancels. A precision common to all of a participant's
drift coefficients cancels out of it. The raw strength slope keeps that
precision: participants who see differences more sharply have steeper slopes
for real and illusory differences alike. The PSE thus measures susceptibility
relative to the participant's own discrimination.

```{r}
imap_dfr(grouplevel, \(g, ill) {
  g$effects |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(Participants = n_distinct(Level), .by = Component) |>
    mutate(Illusion = illusions[ill])
}) |>
  summarise(Participants = first(Participants), .by = Illusion) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Participants per model") |>
  gt_style()
```

## Reliability: D-vour

D-vour, the variability-over-uncertainty ratio (`performance::performance_dvour()`),
compares how much the participants' estimates differ from one another with
how uncertain each of them is:

$$
\text{D-vour} = \frac{\sigma_B^2}{\sigma_B^2 + \mu_{\text{SE}}^2}
$$

where $\sigma_B$ is the standard deviation, across participants, of their
point estimates (posterior medians), and $\mu_{\text{SE}}$ the mean of their
posterior dispersions (MADs). It is 0 when the differences between
participants are no larger than the uncertainty of each, and tends to 1 when
the uncertainty is negligible next to them. Above 0.75 the differences
between participants are at least three times the uncertainty; around 0.5
the two are similar, and the estimates should be used with caution; below
0.5 the uncertainty dominates (the `performance` documentation). It rests on
the estimates alone, so it is itself more reliable with more participants.

```{r}
# D-vour of every effect of every parameter, with the two quantities it is
# made of
dvour_of <- function(tables) {
  imap_dfr(tables, \(g, ill) {
    spread <- as.data.frame(g) |>
      summarise(SD_between = sd(Median), Uncertainty = mean(MAD), .by = c(Component, Parameter))
    performance::performance_dvour(g) |>
      left_join(spread, by = c("Component", "Parameter")) |>
      mutate(Illusion_Type = ill)
  }) |>
    mutate(Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions),
           Model_Parameter = factor(parameter_labels[Component], levels = parameter_labels),
           Effect = Parameter)
}
dvour <- dvour_of(map(grouplevel, "effects")) |>
  mutate(Effect = factor(Effect, levels = igc_grouplevel_effect_names))
```

```{r}
                                        domain = c(0, 1))(pmin(pmax(x, 0), 1))

dvour |>
  arrange(desc(D_vour)) |>
  mutate(Rank = row_number(), .by = Illusion) |>
  select(Illusion, Rank, Model_Parameter, Effect, D_vour, SD_between, Uncertainty) |>

  tab_header(title = "Reliability of the participants' effects",
             subtitle = "D-vour, from the most to the least reliable") |>

             SD_between = "SD between participants", Uncertainty = "Mean uncertainty (MAD)") |>
  fmt_number(D_vour, decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_number(c(SD_between, Uncertainty), decimals = 3) |>
  data_color(D_vour, fn = dvour_colour) |>
```


## Empirical Indices

The usual way to measure individual differences in this task is from the
behaviour directly: how often and how fast a participant responds, overall and
when the illusion works against them, and where their psychometric function
lies. These indices are computed here for every participant, on each illusion,
from the trials the linear models are fitted on (the linear subrange,
`igc_linear_ranges`), so that the next section can relate them to the
participants' model parameters, with the same trials behind both.

```{r}
# The indices, in the order of the tables and plots, with what they are
index_definitions <- tribble(
  ~Index, ~Label, ~Definition,
  "Error_Rate", "Error rate", "Proportion of errors, all trials",
  "RT_Median", "Median RT (s)", "Median RT of the correct responses, all trials",
  "IES", "IES (s)", "Inverse efficiency score: mean RT of the correct responses / proportion correct, all trials",
  "Error_Rate_Incongruent", "Error rate, incongruent", "Proportion of errors when the illusion is incongruent",
  "RT_Median_Incongruent", "Median RT, incongruent (s)", "Median RT of the correct responses when the illusion is incongruent",
  "IES_Incongruent", "IES, incongruent (s)", "Inverse efficiency score when the illusion is incongruent",
  "Illusion_Effect_Errors", "Illusion effect on errors", "Error rate, incongruent − congruent",
  "Illusion_Effect_RT", "Illusion effect on RT (s)", "Median correct RT, incongruent − congruent",
  "PSE", "PSE (difference)", "Point of subjective equality of an incongruent illusion of medium strength (half the strongest of the range): the difference between the targets it cancels (50% errors), from the psychometric function",
  "JND", "JND (difference)", "Just-noticeable difference with no illusion: the difference from 50% to 75% correct, from the psychometric function"
)

index_definitions |>
  select(Index = Label, Definition) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Empirical indices", subtitle = "Per participant and illusion, on the trials of the linear subrange") |>
  gt_style() |>
  cols_align("left")
```

The psychometric function is a logistic regression of each participant's
errors on the difference between the targets and the signed strength of the
illusion (positive when incongruent), on one illusion. Where the error rate is
50%, the participant cannot tell the targets apart. With no illusion, the
slope of the difference gives the JND. Under an incongruent illusion, the
difference at which the errors reach 50% is the point of subjective equality:
the physical difference the illusion cancels, in the units of the difference.
It is taken at half the strongest incongruent strength of the range: at the
strongest, it lies beyond the largest difference shown for about one
participant in six on the Müller-Lyer and Vertical-Horizontal illusions, where
it is extrapolated. The function is linear in both predictors, as a first
approximation. It is left missing when the participant made fewer than five
errors or the fit fails, and when it is degenerate. That covers errors that
do not decrease as the difference grows, and a JND beyond the largest
difference shown (the errors barely depend on the difference). It also covers
a JND below a tenth of the smallest (the errors switch from all to none
between two levels, so the slope is not estimable).

```{r}
# Every participant's trials on each illusion, within its linear subrange
# (the rule of igc_linear_data(), which fit_model.R applies)
ranges <- imap_dfr(igc_linear_ranges, \(r, ill) {
  tibble(Illusion_Type = ill, D_lo = r$difference[1], D_hi = r$difference[2], S_max = r$strength)
})
trials <- map_dfr(1:3, \(i) read.csv(paste0(data_path, "illusion_part", i, ".csv"))) |>
  mutate(Illusion_Difference = abs(Illusion_Difference)) |>
  inner_join(ranges, by = "Illusion_Type") |>
  filter(Illusion_Difference >= D_lo - 1e-9, Illusion_Difference <= D_hi + 1e-9,
         abs(Illusion_Strength) <= S_max + 1e-9)

# A participant's psychometric function on one illusion (see above): the PSE
# of an incongruent illusion of half the strongest strength of the range, and
# the JND, or NA when the function is degenerate
psychometric <- function(d, s_max, d_lo, d_hi) {
  na <- c(PSE = NA_real_, JND = NA_real_)
  if (sum(d$Error) < 5) return(na)
  fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(glm(Error ~ Illusion_Difference + Illusion_Strength,
                                       family = binomial, data = d)),
                  error = \(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit) || !fit$converged) return(na)
  b <- coef(fit)
  if (anyNA(b) || b[["Illusion_Difference"]] >= 0) return(na)
  jnd <- log(3) / -b[["Illusion_Difference"]]
  if (jnd > d_hi || jnd < d_lo / 10) return(na)
  # At the strength of the model-based PSE (igc_pse_strength, server/predictions.R)
  c(PSE = -(b[["(Intercept)"]] + b[["Illusion_Strength"]] * s_max * igc_pse_strength) /
      b[["Illusion_Difference"]],
    JND = jnd)
}

# The inverse efficiency score of some trials (missing if all are errors)
ies <- \(rt, error) if (mean(error) >= 1) NA_real_ else mean(rt[error == 0]) / (1 - mean(error))

empirical <- trials |>
  group_by(Illusion_Type, Participant) |>
  group_modify(\(d, key) {
    inc <- d$Illusion_Strength > 0
    con <- d$Illusion_Strength < 0
    correct <- d$Error == 0
    pf <- psychometric(d, d$S_max[1], d$D_lo[1], d$D_hi[1])
    tibble(Study = sub("^IllusionGame", "", d$Dataset[1]),
           Trials = nrow(d),
           Error_Rate = mean(d$Error),
           RT_Median = median(d$RT[correct]),
           IES = ies(d$RT, d$Error),
           Error_Rate_Incongruent = mean(d$Error[inc]),
           RT_Median_Incongruent = median(d$RT[inc & correct]),
           IES_Incongruent = ies(d$RT[inc], d$Error[inc]),
           Illusion_Effect_Errors = mean(d$Error[inc]) - mean(d$Error[con]),
           Illusion_Effect_RT = median(d$RT[inc & correct]) - median(d$RT[con & correct]),
           PSE = pf[["PSE"]],
           JND = pf[["JND"]])
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions))
```

```{r}
# Per illusion: each index's median and interquartile range across
# participants, and the number of participants it could be computed for
empirical |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(index_definitions$Index), names_to = "Index", values_to = "Value") |>
  summarise(Median = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q1 = quantile(Value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q3 = quantile(Value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            N = sum(!is.na(Value)),
            .by = c(Illusion, Index)) |>
  mutate(Index = factor(index_definitions$Label[match(Index, index_definitions$Index)],
                        levels = index_definitions$Label),
         Summary = sprintf("%.3g [%.3g, %.3g]", Median, Q1, Q3)) |>
  select(Illusion, Index, Summary, N) |>
  arrange(Illusion, Index) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Illusion, values_from = c(Summary, N), names_glue = "{Illusion}__{.value}",
              names_vary = "slowest") |>
  arrange(Index) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Empirical indices", subtitle = "Median [interquartile range] across participants, and N") |>
  tab_spanner_delim("__") |>
  fmt_integer(ends_with("__N")) |>
  gt_style()
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 10

# Their distributions across participants. The axes stop at the 1st and 99th
# percentiles of each index, which the PSE and the JND can exceed by far when a

illusion_colours <- c("Müller-Lyer" = "#E91E63", "Vertical-Horizontal" = "#3F51B5", "Ebbinghaus" = "#009688")
empirical |>

```

The indices are computed for every participant, but only those in a model
(`grouplevel`, above) have parameters to compare them with: for now, the 50
participants of the Müller-Lyer test.

```{r}
imap_dfr(grouplevel, \(g, ill) {
  ids <- unique(as.data.frame(g$effects)$Level)
  tibble(Illusion = illusions[[ill]],
         `In the model` = length(ids),
         `With empirical indices` = sum(ids %in% empirical$Participant[empirical$Illusion_Type == ill]))
}) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Participants in both") |>
  gt_style()
```

## Structure Analysis

How the model's participant-level effects relate to one another and to the
empirical indices: one correlation matrix of every reliable model effect (a
D-vour above `reliable_threshold`) and every empirical index, over the
participants who have both, sorted by hierarchical clustering of the absolute
correlations (`correlation::cor_sort()` on 1 − |r|), so that variables that go
together sit together, whether they rise or fall together.
Once several illusions have a model, their variables enter the same matrix,
joined by participant, which also gives their correlations across illusions.

Two choices:
- The correlations are Spearman's, since several indices are skewed (RTs,
  IES, the PSE and JND).
- Every variable is centred within the participant's study first. The model's
  baselines are deviations from the study's intercept, while the empirical
  indices also carry the differences between studies. Centring both leaves
  the differences between participants of the same study only, on both sides.

The empirical indices have no reliability of their own here, so a weak
correlation with one of them may only mean that it is noisy.

```{r}
# The threshold of D-vour above which a model effect enters the matrix
reliable_threshold <- 0.5
center_within_study <- TRUE

illusion_codes <- c(MullerLyer = "ML", VerticalHorizontal = "VH", Ebbinghaus = "Ebb")
several <- length(grouplevel) > 1

# The reliable model effects, per illusion
reliable_effects <- dvour |>
  filter(D_vour > reliable_threshold) |>
  select(Illusion_Type, Component, Parameter, D_vour)

# Each participant's model effects (posterior medians), long, for the reliable
# ones
model_scores <- imap_dfr(grouplevel, \(g, ill) mutate(as.data.frame(g$effects), Illusion_Type = ill)) |>
  semi_join(reliable_effects, by = c("Illusion_Type", "Component", "Parameter")) |>
  transmute(Participant = Level, Illusion_Type, Source = "Model",
            Variable = paste0(parameter_labels[Component], ": ", Parameter), Value = Median)

# Their empirical indices, on the illusions that have a model, for the
# participants in it
empirical_scores <- empirical |>
  filter(Illusion_Type %in% names(grouplevel)) |>
  semi_join(distinct(model_scores, Participant, Illusion_Type), by = c("Participant", "Illusion_Type")) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(index_definitions$Index), names_to = "Index", values_to = "Value") |>
  transmute(Participant, Illusion_Type, Source = "Empirical",
            Variable = index_definitions$Label[match(Index, index_definitions$Index)], Value)

# Every participant's study, from the empirical indices (every participant
# has them)
studies_of <- distinct(empirical, Participant, Study)

structure_long <- bind_rows(model_scores, empirical_scores) |>
  mutate(Variable = if (several) paste0(illusion_codes[Illusion_Type], " ", Variable) else Variable) |>
  left_join(studies_of, by = "Participant") |>
  mutate(Value = if (center_within_study) Value - mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE) else Value,
         .by = c(Variable, Study))

structure_wide <- structure_long |>
  select(Participant, Variable, Value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Variable, values_from = Value)
```

```{r}
reliable_effects |>
  mutate(Illusion = illusions[Illusion_Type], Parameter_label = parameter_labels[Component]) |>
  arrange(Illusion, desc(D_vour)) |>
  select(Illusion, Parameter = Parameter_label, Effect = Parameter, D_vour) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Illusion") |>
  tab_header(title = "The model effects in the matrix",
             subtitle = paste0("D-vour above ", reliable_threshold, ", with the ",
                               nrow(index_definitions), " empirical indices")) |>
  cols_label(D_vour = "D-vour") |>
  fmt_number(D_vour, decimals = 2) |>
  data_color(D_vour, fn = dvour_colour) |>
  gt_style()
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8.5

# Spearman correlations, pairwise, sorted by hierarchical clustering of their
# absolute values: the distance between two variables is 1 - |r|, so that
# strongly related ones sit together whatever the sign of the relation
# (cor_sort()'s default, (1 - r) / 2, would put r = -.9 as far apart as
# possible). The signed matrix is then shown in that order.
r <- cor(select(structure_wide, -Participant), method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
order_vars <- rownames(correlation::cor_sort(1 - abs(r), distance = "raw"))
r <- r[order_vars, order_vars]
sources <- distinct(structure_long, Variable, Source)

as.data.frame(r) |>
  rownames_to_column("Variable1") |>
  pivot_longer(-Variable1, names_to = "Variable2", values_to = "r") |>
  mutate(Label = if_else(Variable1 == Variable2, "", sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", sprintf("%.2f", r))),
         Variable1 = factor(Variable1, levels = rev(order_vars)),
         Variable2 = factor(Variable2, levels = order_vars)) |>
  ggplot(aes(Variable2, Variable1, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Label, colour = abs(r) > 0.6), size = 2.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#1565C0", mid = "white", high = "#C62828", limits = c(-1, 1), name = "rho") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey20", "TRUE" = "white")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Structure of the model effects and the empirical indices",
       subtitle = paste0("Spearman correlations, ", nrow(structure_wide), " participants",
                         if (center_within_study) ", centred within study" else "",
                         "; ", sum(sources$Source == "Model"), " reliable model effects (D-vour > ",
                         reliable_threshold, ") and ", sum(sources$Source == "Empirical"),
                         " empirical indices")) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank())
```
